notes:
Summary: enterprise procurement focused on Dedicated capacity with hard throughput guarantees. Ironbloom runs customer-facing chat + real-time fraud scoring. Priority = determinism and predictable cost per sustained token rate. Currently negotiating min tokens/sec guarantees, concurrency caps, and burst policies.

Key ask (Ironbloom):
- Sustained baseline: 50,000 tokens/sec (aggregate across service) with <250ms p95 for requests <=512 tokens.
- Concurrency cap: support 600 concurrent live sessions with KV cache locality; elastic burst to 1,000,000 tokens/sec for 120s to absorb spikes during market opens.
- Guaranteed capacity isolation: no noisy-neighbor impact, reserved GPUs with strict tenancy.
- Failure/fallback: automatic fallback to smaller model under constrained conditions with defined QoS and routing policy.

Redwood proposal (current):
- Baseline guaranteed min tokens/sec: 40,000 sustained.
- Concurrency: recommended 500 session target with documented performance curves; can add burst pool (best-effort) up to 900,000 tokens/sec for 60s.
- Reserved hardware: proposal includes 8xA100-equivalent nodes (customer-dedicated pool) + 2-node warm standby for failover.
- SLA credits: service credits tiered; dispute over cap at 30% of monthly invoice.

Negotiation notes / back-and-forth:
- 2026-01-29 (discovery call): Ironbloom engineering laid out traffic profile: 95% of requests are <=256 tokens; 2% are large (up to 2k tokens) during batch reporting. Emphasized sub-200ms p95 requirement for short requests.
- 2026-02-10 (technical deep dive w/ SE Diego): validated perf curves on equivalent load generator; Redwood demoed steady-state 45k tokens/sec on proposed config with p95 ~220ms. Ironbloom asked for written perf plan and kernel choices.
- 2026-02-18 (pricing & SLA call): legal + finance from IB asked for stronger guaranteed baseline (50k) and explicit definition of "burst" (duration, preemption behavior). IB flagged need for hard concurrency caps per API key to bound tail latency.
- 2026-02-25 (SLA wording review): Redwood sent draft SLA; IB markups: (1) replace "best-effort" burst language with defined burst pool and throttling behavior; (2) include right to audit capacity utilization quarterly; (3) require 99.5% uptime on dedicated pool.
- 2026-03-04 (on-site + cloud ops workshop): capacity planning spreadsheet shared (drive link above). IB provided internal load histograms. SE proposed option B (10 reserved nodes) to hit 50k sustained with comfortable headroom.

Technical concerns from IB engineering:
- How token/sec maps to reserved GPU count across model variants (quantized vs fp16). Need deterministic mapping matrix in SOW.
- KV cache warm-up: cold starts during failover may violate latency SLO; want pre-warmed standby or rapid KV handoff policy.
- Burst enforcement: IB worried burst may be preempted mid-request; requests must complete at least to last committed token.

Commercial asks from IB procurement:
- Price floor if we commit to 50k tokens/sec baseline; discount tiers for higher committments.
- SLA credit cap reduction (they want uncapped/meaningful credits for sustained miss >7 days — Redwood pushed back).

Open items to resolve (actionable):
- Redwood to produce SOW appendix: mapping table tokens/sec -> reserved GPU numbers for requested models and seq lengths (due 2026-03-10).
- Legal teams to agree on burst definition: duration, throttling vs drop, precedence over other customers (due 2026-03-18).
- Final pricing call to reconcile cost delta between 8-node vs 10-node proposal (schedule week of 2026-03-15).

Internal AE notes / negotiation strategy:
- prioritize securing 3-yr commit with annual review; offer tiered credits if IB accepts 10-node config.
- propose a signed "performance appendix" that lists deterministic mapping; reduces procurement friction.
- allow a one-time test burst event (simulated market open) as part of onboarding acceptance tests.

Quotes / direct lines:
- CTO (Arjun Mehta): "We need operator-grade predictability — if the model trips during market open we lose customers. Credits don't fix lost revenue."
- Head of Ops (Lina Park): "If you can give us a firm mapping of tokens/sec to GPUs and a test run, we'll move to signature."

POC / Acceptance criteria (agreed in principle):
- Onboarding tests: three 10-minute sustained runs at 55k tokens/sec with p95 <250ms for <=512 tokens.
- Failover test: simulated node loss with KV recovery <60s and no request loss for in-flight sessions.
- Burstable event test: single 2-minute spike to 900k tokens/sec with defined throttling behavior and metrics capture.

Follow-ups scheduled:
- 2026-03-08: Redwood SE to deliver SOW appendix (tokens->GPU mapping).
- 2026-03-15: Final pricing + SLA call (Maya + IB procurement + Diego + Redwood legal).
- 2026-03-22: Onboarding window for acceptance testing (tentative).

Short choppy CRM snippets:

- "Legal: tighten burst wording; require quarterly audit rights."
- "Ops: want pre-warmed standby nodes (not cold spin-up)."

Relevant artifacts: pricing spreadsheet, perf-run logs (attached to drive), redacted Fireflies transcripts. Jira tickets RBW-1248 (performance regression investigation on demo run) and RBW-1287 (SLA appendix draft).

Recommended AE playbook: prioritize appendix + test window. Offer commercial sweetener (3 months free for first year) if IB signs 3-yr commit and accepts 10-node reserved config.
